_doc: Community-maintained rate card. USD per million tokens, from each vendor's public price list. Multipliers apply to the model's own input rate; a model may set its own `cache_read_mult` when the vendor's cache-hit discount isn't the 0.1x default. `window` names a peak/off-peak schedule in `windows` — a pricing shape that Chinese vendors use and Western trackers ignore. See docs/specs/Cost-Estimation.md and docs/specs/Peak-Off-Peak-Pricing.md.
_contributing: Rates go stale. Correcting one is the easiest useful PR in this repo: edit the entry, move `_verified_on`, cite the vendor page in the PR body. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
_windows_doc: Peak/off-peak schedules. `peak_utc` is a list of [start_hour, end_hour) in UTC; `days` restricts to weekdays (1=Mon..7=Sun) when present. `off_peak_mult` scales the listed (peak) rate outside those hours. A model without a `window` is billed flat, all day. Local-time schedules are converted to UTC here on purpose so the engine never has to know a timezone.

deepseek-v4.note: Effective 2026-08-16. Listed rates are PEAK; every other hour bills at half. Applies to V4 Flash and V4 Pro.

deepseek-legacy.note: The V3/R1-generation window: 16:30-00:30 UTC discounted. Approximated to whole hours; kept for historical events only.

glm-coding.note: Z.ai peak is 14:00-18:00 UTC+8 on weekdays only = 06:00-10:00 UTC. Weekends are entirely off-peak.

vendors._doc: How each vendor lets you pay less for the SAME tokens. Two mechanisms, and they are not the same thing. `window` (see above) is the clock: the price changes by the hour and you do nothing but run later. `batch_mult` is the queue: you accept a slower turnaround (typically within 24h) and the vendor charges a fraction of the interactive rate. Both reward the same habit — stop paying interactive prices for work nobody is watching.
vendors._contributing: A vendor listed here has been checked; a vendor absent from here has NOT been, and the figures say so rather than implying it charges flat. Do not add an entry asserting `no cheaper lane` unless you have looked at the vendor's pricing page — 'we never checked' and 'there is nothing there' look identical to a reader and only one of them is true. Cite the page in the PR and move `_verified_on`, exactly as for a model rate.

anthropic.note: Flat by the hour. Message Batches API bills 0.5x for work that can wait.

openai.note: Flat by the hour. Batch API bills 0.5x, results within 24h.

google.note: Flat by the hour. Gemini batch mode bills 0.5x.

alibaba.note: No vendor-wide batch_mult set — the discount is real but per-model, not universal. Batch calls (where a model supports them) bill input and output at 0.5x real-time, mutually exclusive with the context-cache discount. qwen3-max shows the batch tag on Model Studio's regional tables; qwen3-coder-plus, qwen3-coder-flash and qwen3-plus do not. Verified 2026-08-20: alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/models

baidu.note: No vendor-wide batch_mult set. Qianfan does offer batch inference, but at 0.4x (60% off), not the 0.5x other vendors use — and it does NOT cover ernie-5.0, the only Baidu model in this file. Batch is limited to the ERNIE-4.5-Turbo family, a DeepSeek-V3.2 resale, and InternVL3, none of which are priced here yet. Verified 2026-08-20: cloud.baidu.com/doc/QIANFAN/s/qm3ie59jf

bytedance.note: No vendor-wide batch_mult set. Volcengine's Doubao-Seed-2.0 and Seed-2.1 both bill batch inference at exactly 0.5x (confirmed on the console); Seed-Evolving and Seed-Character show no batch option. Which Seed generation doubao-pro/doubao-seed-code in this file map to on Volcengine's current catalog is unconfirmed — do not apply 0.5x to either until that's checked. Verified 2026-08-20: volcengine.com/pricing?product=ark_subscription

minimax.note: Checked, nothing found. No batch or off-peak lane anywhere on the pay-as-you-go or Token Plan pages — only prompt-caching discounts and a 1.5x 'Priority' premium (faster admission, not cheaper). Verified 2026-08-20: platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/pricing-paygo

moonshot.note: No vendor-wide batch_mult set. Kimi's own Batch Inference page states 0.6x (60% of standard) explicitly for kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.5 only — kimi-k3 (also priced in this file) is excluded, so a single vendor-level multiplier would misprice it. Verified 2026-08-20: platform.kimi.com/docs/pricing/batch

stepfun.note: Checked, nothing found. No batch or off-peak lane on the pricing/rate-limits page — only cache-hit vs cache-miss input pricing and top-up-based rate-limit tiers. Verified 2026-08-20: platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/pricing/details

tencent.note: Checked, nothing found. No batch or off-peak lane on Hunyuan's pricing page — only free resource packages and prepaid/postpaid billing. Page also flags Tencent is mid-migration to a new 'TokenHub' console. Verified 2026-08-20: cloud.tencent.com/document/product/1729

xai.note: No vendor-wide batch_mult set. xAI's own pricing page states Batch API bills 0.8x (20% off) for grok-4.3, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning and grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 only — the flagship grok-4.6/grok-4.5 and grok-build-0.1 get none. Which of these grok-4/grok-code-fast in this file correspond to on xAI's current catalog is unconfirmed; do not apply 0.8x to either until that's checked. Verified 2026-08-20: docs.x.ai/developers/pricing

codex-auto-review.note: guardian subagent — billed as the base model

kimi-k3.note: cache-hit input $0.30/M -> 0.1x, matches the global default

_aliases_doc: Vendor model ids seen in transcripts that map onto a canonical entry above. Keeps the rate card small when a vendor ships five ids for one price point.
